source_readme:
MOVATE AI OPERATIONS INTELLIGENCE — SYNTHETIC DATA V1
Generated 2026-10-22; deterministic random seed 20261022; modeled window 2026-07-01 through 2026-10-15.

IMPORTANT: All people, contacts, tickets, financial values, audits, outcomes and events are entirely invented. Program names are taken as scenario labels from the supplied worksheets, not from Movate systems. This dataset is NOT authentic Movate or client operational data; it does not prove customer relationships or business outcomes.

SOURCE TRACEABILITY
source_opportunities.csv preserves source workbook filename, original row and sheet, exact opportunity descriptions, proposed solution text and impact claims. opportunity_catalog.csv deduplicates the repeated opportunity titles while retaining source IDs. Original claimed impacts are source proposals, not observed outcomes.

DATA MODEL
programs -> employees -> interactions -> tickets / qa_audits -> coaching_actions. Interactions optionally reference knowledge_articles. Employees also join to training_enrollments -> trainers/courses, sales_leads (via interactions), hr_cases, hr_onboarding and employee_recognitions. opportunity_catalog -> solution_alternatives -> scenario_estimates. relational_map.csv specifies key joins. daily_program_kpis.csv is aggregated from interactions.

SYNTHETIC LOGIC AND ASSUMPTIONS
12,000 interactions across four scenario programs; 240 agents; contact outcomes, AHT, CSAT and SLA flags generated by probability distributions and issue complexity. QA sample is 2,200 audited interactions. Coachings are produced only for audit scores below 85. Training enrollments are independent events; compare same employees and valid time periods to analyze associations. Financial scenario calculations use assumed hours, hourly costs, up-front implementation spend, monthly costs and improvement rates; these are not validated predictions. USD is a demo accounting convention.

PRIVACY / DEMO LIMITS
All employee names marked [SYN]. No authentic PII or real client records. HR disciplinary actions require restricted access, human review and immutable audit trails. Automated QA scoring and speech analytics should be treated as candidate capabilities, not demonstrated model accuracy. Correlation of training/QA is not causal proof. Non-applicable data and source-level impact estimates must not be represented as real KPIs.

DEMO RECOMMENDATION
Local React + FastAPI + DuckDB/SQLite or Streamlit + DuckDB. Deterministic SQL for measured KPIs, retrieval across source opportunity descriptions, LLM to synthesize alternative decisions, scenario calculator using explicit model assumptions, per-answer evidence links to record IDs, access-controlled HR views, and human-approval gates.

REVIEW PROCEDURE
1 Check source_opportunities and opportunity_catalog for workbook-row coverage and repetition.
2 Inspect relational_map and run foreign-key tests.
3 Recompute daily_program_kpis from interactions.
4 Filter program -> employee -> interaction -> audit -> coaching and time-bound training.
5 Compare solution_alternatives and scenario_estimates while reviewing assumptions.

Manual & Fragmented Training Reporting

Time-consuming manual consolidation across teams/geos
High risk of data errors and inconsistencies
Delayed insights (reports are backward-looking, not real-time)
Limited ability to link training outcomes to business KPIs (QA, CSAT, AHT, productivity)
Reduced credibility of Training as a data-driven function

1. Automated Reporting & Dashboard
Implement BI tools like Power BI or Tableau
Auto-pull data from LMS, HRIS, QA tools, and operations systems
Real-time dashboards for stakeholders (Ops, Clients, Leadership)

2. Unified Training Data Model
Create a single source of truth across geos
Automate data pipelines instead of manual file merging

3. AI-Driven Insights & Predictive Analytics
Use tools like ChatGPT or embedded AI in BI tools to:
Generate insights summaries (“What changed this week?”)
Identify at-risk trainees early
Correlate training with performance outcomes

4. Self-Service Reporting for Stakeholders
Enable Operations and Clients to access dashboards directly
Reduce ad hoc report requests to Training teams
Role-based views (Trainer, Manager, Executive)

5. Automated Report Generation
Schedule auto-generated weekly/monthly reports
Use AI to convert dashboards into executive summaries
Eliminate manual PPT/Excel reporting cycles

60–80% reduction in manual reporting effort
Real-time visibility for faster decision-making
Stronger linkage between training and business performance
Increased credibility of Training as a strategic, data-driven function
